source.name: Open-Meteo elevation API
source.upstreamModels: A downsampled global elevation model, ~90 m posting (derived from SRTM and coarser sources). The ~90 m figure is measured on the returned grid, not advertised: the API reports no resolution, and asking for a finer lattice only duplicates values. See grid.resolutionLonM/LatM.
source.note: Verified against Everest and open-ocean control points on every run. The AWS elevation-tiles-prod bucket was tested and rejected: it returns HTTP 200 with non-terrarium pixels that decode to nonsense (Everest ~1e6 m).

grid.resolutionNote: Measured from the deduplicated grid. The source is a ~90 m global model; requesting a finer lattice duplicates values rather than resolving them.

caveats: Sampled, not a survey product: ~90 m postings resampled onto the 5 m analysis grid. The 5 m grid is the analysis convention, not the data resolution, and the ~90 m figure is the measured one.
Orthometric (mPD), not ellipsoidal. No vertical datum shift applied.
No bare-earth correction. If vegetation/structures bias this upward, a deficit estimate would be biased too.
Sinks are not filled and there is no flow routing; the wet grid fills by water-surface level, not by routing water downhill.
